notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Kickoff with Sandra Kowalczyk. Replacing a 20-year-old MRP and finance system at a single, tightly integrated plant. Using the firm's standard phased approach: finance module first, then inventory, then production scheduling. Budget $1.9M.

notes.author: Nadia Farouk
notes.text: Finance module live on the new ERP while inventory still runs on the old MRP. Nightly sync between the two built as a stopgap.

notes.author: Nadia Farouk
notes.text: Serious problem: inventory valuations disagree between systems by ~$310k. Every work order touches both inventory and costing, so the sync breaks daily. Two sources of truth; the shop floor has stopped trusting either.

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Ben Adeyemi escalated: two late shipments to a defense prime traced to MRP/ERP mismatch. Sandra: "Your phased plan is costing us customers." Phased approach is not working here — modules are too interdependent at a single site.

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Re-planned: roll finance back behind a freeze and move to a single-weekend cutover of all modules, preceded by three full dress rehearsals with real data snapshots and a hard rollback criterion.

notes.author: Nadia Farouk
notes.text: Dress rehearsals 1-3 complete; rehearsal 3 ran clean in 31 hours. Julia Marsh built a cutover runbook with named owners per step.

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Cutover weekend succeeded. Plant running on the new ERP Monday morning; zero late shipments in the following 6 weeks. Lesson: phasing assumed modules could live apart, but here they could not.

simulation.lesson: A phased, module-by-module migration can fail badly when the modules are tightly interdependent at a single site: running old and new systems side by side creates two sources of truth that break daily. In that situation a single, well-rehearsed cutover — with several full dress rehearsals on real data snapshots and a hard rollback criterion — worked better than phasing.
simulation.why: Tightly coupled modules cannot run apart; interim syncs create conflicting records and erode trust.
simulation.conditions: Single site, highly interdependent modules, every transaction spans multiple modules.
